s1-armstrong-numbers.trick: Count decimal digits, then sum each digit raised to that count; compare with the original number.

s1-check-for-prime.trick: Check divisors only up to √n. The linked GFG minimum-jumps page is unrelated; the CN/TUF links match this prime-check lesson.

s1-check-palindrome.trick: Reverse only the last half of the digits, then compare both halves.

s1-count-digits.trick: Count decimal digits by repeated division; zero has one digit. The linked GFG task instead counts nonzero digits that divide the original number.

s1-counting-frequencies-of-array-element.trick: Increment a hash-map count for each value; the map is the frequency table.

s1-gcd-or-hcf.trick: Euclid's algorithm repeatedly replaces (a,b) with (b,a mod b). Normalize signs so the HCF is nonnegative.

s1-print-all-divisors.trick: Divisors of n come in pairs around √n. The linked GFG task instead sums divisors of every integer from 1 to n.
s1-print-all-divisors.time: O(√n + d log d) to list; O(n) for linked sum
s1-print-all-divisors.space: O(d) for list; O(1) for linked sum

s1-reverse-a-number.trick: Move one digit at a time into the reversed number, checking the 32-bit boundary before multiplying by ten.

s1-understand-recursion-by-print-somethi.trick: Every call does one unit of work, reduces n by one, and stops at zero; the base case prevents infinite recursion.

s1-print-name-n-times-using-recursion.trick: Print once, then recurse for the remaining n-1 copies; stop when n is zero.

s1-print-1-to-n-using-recursion.trick: Recurse to n-1 before outputting n, so the values appear in ascending order.

s1-print-n-to-1-using-recursion.trick: Output n before recursing to n-1, giving descending order.

s1-sum-of-first-n-numbers.trick: The lesson sums 1 through n recursively. The linked GFG task asks for the sum of cubes, equal to (n(n+1)/2)².
s1-sum-of-first-n-numbers.time: O(n) for recursive sum; O(1) for linked cubes
s1-sum-of-first-n-numbers.space: O(n) call stack for recursive sum; O(1) for cubes

s1-reverse-an-array.trick: Swap the outer pair and move both pointers inward until they cross.

s1-check-if-a-string-is-palindrome-or-no.trick: Compare from both ends. The linked LeetCode Valid Palindrome variant ignores punctuation and letter case.

s1-fibonacci-number.trick: Keep only the previous two Fibonacci values; each new value is their sum. Assume n is nonnegative and the answer fits long long.

s1-find-the-highest-lowest-frequency-ele.trick: Count frequencies, then choose the highest and lowest counts (smaller value on ties). The linked LeetCode page asks a different frequency problem.

s1-user-input-output.trick: Read input with >> and print with <<. This is an input/output lesson; the linked GFG autocomplete page is a different problem.

s1-data-types.trick: Select a type by the kind and range of data. For the linked practice task, map each type name to the byte count expected by that judge.

s1-if-else-statements.trick: Compare a and b; only the first matching branch runs. This solves the linked if-else practice task.

s1-switch-statement.trick: Switch on the choice: 1 uses circle area πr², and 2 uses rectangle area length×breadth, as in the linked practice task.

s1-what-are-arrays-strings.trick: An array-like vector stores indexed values; a string stores indexed characters. Both use zero-based indices.

s1-for-loops.trick: Use a for loop when the range or iteration count is known in advance.

s1-while-loops.trick: Use a while loop while a condition remains true; update its state to ensure it terminates.

s1-functions-pass-by-reference-and-value.trick: The linked task adds 1 to the copied value a and 2 to the referenced value b; only b changes in the caller.

s1-time-complexity-learn-basics-and-then.trick: Count how often the dominant operation runs; nested full loops multiply, while consecutive loops add.

s1-patterns.trick: For each row, print a predictable number of symbols; nested loops turn the pattern rule into code.

s1-c-stl.trick: C++ STL containers and algorithms provide tested building blocks; sort, binary search, and hash maps are common DSA tools.
s1-c-stl.time: O(n log n) for sorting; O(log n) search

s1-java-collections.trick: This lesson is about Java collections; the C++ equivalents are vector for ArrayList, unordered_set for HashSet, and unordered_map for HashMap.

s1-factorial-of-n-numbers.trick: Generate factorials 1!, 2!, ... only while the next multiplication stays at most the limit.
s1-factorial-of-n-numbers.time: O(k), k factorials not exceeding limit

s1-hashing-theory.trick: Hash tables map keys to buckets, giving expected constant-time insert and lookup. Use them to count frequencies.
